title: Unify sub-navigation patterns across Prompt and Run Insights pages
description:
The prompt conversation page and Run Insights page use completely different navigation patterns:

**Run Insights:**
- Page title 'Run Insights' as h1
- Sub-nav tabs (Overview | Status) with underline active indicator
- Clear visual hierarchy

**Prompt conversation:**
- No page title
- Inline header buttons (New Prompt | History | feature)
- 'feature' is a muted label, not a tab
- No active state indicators

## Design Requirements

**MUST derive from site/ design system (Amber Circuit theme):**
- Reference site/src/style.css for colors, typography, spacing
- Use amber as primary accent, cyan as secondary
- Match card styling, hover states, and visual patterns from marketing site

**Apply frontend design skills:**
- Create a unified SectionHeader component both pages can use
- Left side: context/breadcrumb (page title or path like '📁 / project / feature')
- Right side: actions/tabs with consistent styling
- Use underline indicators for active states (matching site pattern)

**Proposed pattern:**
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [Context/Breadcrumb]                        [Actions/Tabs] │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- Prompt page: breadcrumb left, History + Preview actions right
- Run Insights: title left, Overview + Status tabs right

title: Design Rust cross-agent session history capability
description: Fresh implementation on feat/session-memory-rust. Independent Rust session-history capability within an extensible platform, accessed through CLI, MCP, and REST. Confirmed: live capture first, no day-one backfill; future importers must use the same ingestion boundary. Start on one device; design for later centralized storage/retrieval across devices. Entries archive user/agent messages and tool calls/results with stable source identity and occurred_at/recorded_at times. Confirmed Git design: lightweight per-entry checkpoint references; baseline at session start and checkpoints after completed tool calls and turn boundaries; preserve actual observed file changes in self-contained compressed content-addressed storage, including pre-existing dirty state, staged/unstaged distinctions, new non-ignored files, deletions, and binary changes. Capture eagerly, generate/retrieve diffs on demand; retain enough content to work after reset, branch switch, or removal of original checkout. Checkpoints show observed state, not guaranteed agent attribution or every intermediate filesystem write. Confirmed future direction: a centralized endpoint for cross-device session writes and reads. Proposed foundations: globally unique archive session/entry/checkpoint IDs, persistent device and source-instance identity, source IDs scoped to their origin, device-local workspace identity separate from logical project identity, idempotent ingestion, explicit entry relationships/order independent of wall-clock timestamps, content hashes and complete checkpoint manifests, and transport-independent application operations. Keep database handles and absolute local paths out of public contracts. Defer remote transport/sync/auth policy until needed. Open decisions: first live integration, exact API and Git capture coverage, local storage layout, and fresh workspace bootstrap. Research: original NDJSON persistence redesign in 7316177; simplified MemoryStore in 2511528; current conversation hooks buffer text rather than archive all entries. Validate full design with user before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: User-approved module boundary, ingestion approach, session/entry identity and provenance model, storage strategy, transport scope, and first end-to-end implementation slice.
notes: User uses OpenCode and Cursor: both are initial live-capture targets. Treat Cursor desktop Agent Chat as the working assumption. Official docs checked 2026-09-09: OpenCode supports message.updated, message.part.updated/removed, session lifecycle and tool.execute.before/after; requires a small JS/TS plugin bridge to Rust. Cursor supports beforeSubmitPrompt, afterAgentResponse, preToolUse/postToolUse/postToolUseFailure, stop, subagent hooks, and sessionStart/sessionEnd; command hooks receive JSON plus conversation_id/generation_id and optional transcript_path. Cursor session lifecycle hooks are fire-and-forget; baseline timing must use an awaited pre-action hook, not assume sessionStart completes before edits. Transcript availability is optional, and native event IDs are not universal; adapter implementation must define durable delivery IDs without deduplicating legitimate identical messages. Retain source event identities and payloads, normalize into shared records, and explicitly report capture coverage/partial checkpoints. Verify installed-client behavior through one real conversation per integration, including prompts, assistant messages, successful/failed tools, shell edits, and cross-client retrieval. Sources: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ and https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks .
